verdict: Roblox grew revenue 39% to $1.44B and bookings 43% to $1.73B as daily users hit 132 million, but heavy spending — including a $57M legal settlement charge — kept it at a $248M loss.

kpis.label: Bookings
kpis.note: +43% YoY — the cash players actually spent

segments.name: Platform revenue
segments.note: Sales of Robux (the platform's virtual currency) and subscriptions, recognized gradually over the ~27 months players are expected to keep spending. The cash collected upfront ('bookings') was $1,731M.

opex.name: Developer exchange fees
opex.note: The cut paid out to creators when players spend Robux in their games — Roblox raised creator pay rates in September 2025.

opex.name: Infrastructure and trust & safety
opex.note: Servers and computing (including AI) plus the safety operation that polices the platform — Q1 included the rollout of age-checking for users.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform, tools and AI features.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference. Costs ran to about $120 per $100 of revenue — the extra is the loss, covered by cash the company already had.

takeaways.title: The audience kept growing
takeaways.text: Daily active users rose 35% to 132 million and hours engaged jumped 43% to 31 billion — even as a Russia platform ban and the age-check rollout tempered growth.

takeaways.title: Bookings jumped 43%
takeaways.text: Bookings — Robux cash sales — reached $1,731M, and free cash flow was $596M despite the accounting loss: players pay upfront, and $275M of costs were stock pay, not cash.

takeaways.title: A legal charge sits in the loss
takeaways.text: GAAP results include $57M of legal settlement expenses from negotiations with U.S. states over youth consumer-protection and digital-safety matters. Excluding them and other non-cash items, Adjusted EBITDA was $99M.

oneTimers: GAAP expenses include $57M of legal settlement expenses related to settlement negotiations with certain states regarding youth-related consumer protection and digital safety matters — Roblox excludes them from its Adjusted EBITDA of $99M.

Revenue is not the cash in: bookings were $1,731M but revenue was $1,442M. Roblox defers most bookings and recognizes them over the 27-month average paying-user lifetime, so reported revenue lags the cash by design.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$47M: $55M of interest earned on Roblox's investment pile, minus $10M of interest expense, plus $2M of other income.
